taxonomic_note: Current Kew accepts Rhus virens and recognizes var. virens and var. australis. The learner remains species-level.
look_here_first: Look for leathery evergreen foliage: alternate compound leaves usually have only 5–9 thick, smooth-edged leaflets that are glossy dark green above.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — UT PRC Purola natural flora; Travis — UT PRC herbarium index; Comal — Lindheimer isotype from New Braunfels.

best_field_traits: evergreen to semi-evergreen large shrub or small tree
odd-pinnate leaves usually with only 5–9 thick leathery leaflets
leaflets entire and glossy dark green above
flattened red drupes are covered with red hairs
morphology_keys.habit: Evergreen to semi-evergreen shrub or small tree.
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Usually 5–9 thick leathery entire leaflets; glossy dark green above, duller beneath.
morphology_keys.stem: Young rachises and stems often reddish.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Compact branched clusters of small creamy-white flowers.
morphology_keys.fruit: Flattened red drupes with red hairs.
morphology_keys.joey_field_observation: Joey Santore's West Texas pinyon-pine video includes an exact Rhus virens flowering branch frame showing inflorescence plus compound-leaf context.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Flameleaf sumac has many narrow leaflets on a strongly winged rachis and is deciduous. Fragrant sumac has exactly 3 often lobed/toothed leaflets and stays low.
